full_judgment:
ATM Afzal CJ : This appeal by leave arises out of a proceeding under section 95 and 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and is directed against the judgment and order dated 5th June 1990 passed by a Divisor Bench of the High Court Division (Barisal Session) in Writ Petition No. 29 of 1988 making the Rule absolute and declaring that the order of the Additional Commissioner, Khulna Division dated 24-3-1988 in Redemption Appeal No. 213 of 1985 was of no legal effect. 

 4. It appears from the Paper Book that the proceeding started by the appellant under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for redemption of the disputed land was dismissed by the CO (Revenue), Bakergonj by his order dated 3-2-1983 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 922 BK/73-74 and appeal from the said order was also dismissed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) on 1-7-1985 and upon a further appeal the Additional Commissioner, Khulna by his order dated 24-3-1988 allowed the appeal and ordered for redemption of the land as prayed for by the appellant in his Miscellaneous case. As already noticed the order of the Additional Commissioner, Khulna Division was set aside by the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No. 29 of 1988. 

 5. The High Court Division in the impugned judgment observed that as the date of reconveyance expired on 1-3-1972 before the President's Order No. 88 of 1972 came into force on 3-8-1972, the transaction on the basis of Annexures "A" & "B" to the writ petition could not be treated as a mortgage transaction in the light of the decision in Bangladesh vs. Haji Abdul Gani Biswas 32 DLR (AD) 233 and the appellant was not entitled to get back the case land on the basis of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 6. Leave was granted to consider the submission that the High Court Division upon an erroneous view of section 95 and 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the decision referred to above as also the facts of the case erred in holding that the appellant was not entitled to get back the case land. 

 7. There is no dispute that the appellant sold the land to respondent No. 1 by kabala dated 24-6-1967 and the agreement for reconveyance of the said land executed on the same day stipulated a period of 4 (four) years from the said date, that is to say, the time for reconveyance expired on 23-6-1971. The question for consideration is whether the aforesaid transaction is attracted by section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 95A. Treatment of Certain Transaction as Usufructuary Mortgage. Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, any transfer of a holding or of portion or share thereof, either by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey or where the transferor receives from the transferee any consideration and the transferee acquires the right to possess, and to enjoy the usufruct of, such holding or portion or share thereof for a specified period in lieu of such consideration, shall notwithstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years and the provisions of section 95 shall apply to such transfer whether made before or after the date of commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy(Second Amendment) Order, 1972 (President's Order 88/72). 

 Our conclusions, therefore, are that the President's Order Nos. 88 and 136 of 1972 and No. 24 of 1973 are all valid legislation for effecting necessary amendments in the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and those laws cannot be attacked on the ground of ultra vires; (2) any transfer of a holding or part thereof by a raiyat either by way of out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey or where the transferor receives from the transferee any consideration and transferee acquires the right to possess and enjoy the usufruct, shall notwithstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period of maximum 7 years and the provisions of section 95(4) and (5) shall apply to such transfers; (3) and such transfers are not to be understood in the light of the Transfer of Property Act because those are to be understood in the light of the enactment in question: (4) those transactions which are subsisting on the date of promulgation of President's Order No. 88 of 1972 are hit by section 95A including the transaction entered into by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey, made whether before or after the promulgation of President's Order No. 88 of 1972: and (5) as for the transactions which are not alive before the promulgation of President's Order No. 88 of 1972 they are concluded by the transactions past and closed. 

 13. Mr. Khan also argued that since the transaction in question has been found to be a complete usufructuary mortgage under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the appellant was entitled to seek for redemption of the said mortgage and the doctrine of 'transaction past and closed' did not apply. In support of his contention he referred to Abu Bakkar vs. Nazir Ahmed 34 DLR (AD) 237. We have perused the said decision and found that the same does not help the appellant. In that case plaintiff-appellant filed a suit in 1964 for redemption of the suit land which was transferred by him to the defendant-respondent under a registered instrument dated 11 November, 1953. Question arose whether the document: in question was a kot mortgage or an out and out sale with a condition for reconveyance on repayment of the consideration within a period of 5 years. The trial Court held the transaction to be an out and out sale and dismissed the suit but on appeal the learned Subordinate Judge found the transaction to be a complete usufructuary mortgage, the consideration of which was already satisfied by the usufruct of the land and accordingly, decreed the suit for redemption. The decree was, however, set aside by the High Court Division taking the view that the suit was barred by limitation as well as by the doctrine of transaction past and closed. Leave was granted to consider whether the suit was barred by limitation as well as by the doctrine of transaction past and closed as held by the High Court Division.
